result:
All questions researched. Answers below.

---

**h01** — S3 presign runner — every 12 hours (plus one immediate run at startup) — wired in `server/server.go:162-171` (inside `startBackgroundRunners`, called from `Start` at `server/server.go:129`)

- Component: `s3presign.Runner` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:16`), work done in `CheckAndPresign` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:47`) which re-presigns S3 object URLs whose presign is older than 4 days (5-day expiry) and writes the new `Reference` back via `UpdateAttachment`.
- Schedule: `runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`), ticker loop in `Run` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:29-41`); `RunOnce(ctx)` is also called synchronously once at startup (`server/server.go:163`).

**h02** — delivery function: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120` (actual send at `:152` via `safeClient.Do(req)`); protection: SSRF guard `safeDialContext` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:59-77`

- `safeClient` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:32-37`) is an `http.Client` whose `Transport.DialContext` is `safeDialContext`; it resolves the host and rejects any address in a reserved/private range via `isReservedIP` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:70-74`). Blocking at dial time also defeats DNS rebinding. Async path: `PostAsync` (`:184`) enqueues onto a 128-slot channel drained by 4 goroutines started in `init` (`:42-55`).

**h03** — abstraction package: `internal/idp` (`internal/idp/idp.go`); implementation package: `internal/idp/oauth2` (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go`)

- `internal/idp` is the shared abstraction layer — it declares `IdentityProviderUserInfo` (`internal/idp/idp.go:3-8`), the provider-neutral result type. It declares no Go `interface`.
- Only OAuth2 ships: `oauth2.IdentityProvider` with `NewIdentityProvider` (`internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:27`), `ExchangeToken` (`:47`, incl. PKCE), `UserInfo` (`:83`). The proto enum only carries `OAUTH2` as well; consumed at `server/router/api/v1/auth_service_sso.go`.

**h04** — no; `mysql.NewDB` is referenced exactly once in the whole repo

- Only construction site: `store/db/db.go:22` inside `NewDBDriver`'s `case "mysql"`. A repo-wide grep for `mysql.NewDB` returns that line only. (For contrast, `sqlite.NewDB` *is* constructed directly outside the factory, in tests: `store/demo_seed_test.go:24` and `store/deployment_config_test.go:416` — MySQL has no such direct use.) The `mysql` package is otherwise only reached through the `store.Driver` interface.

**h05** — explicit Go code (per-driver), not a database rule

- Explicit deletes, two of them per driver — by memo content-id and by creator:
  - `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:381-403` (`deleteReactionsByContentIDsTx`, `deleteReactionsByCreatorTx`), sequenced in `deleteUserTargetsTx` at `store/db/sqlite/user_delete.go:91-96`
  - `store/db/mysql/user_delete.go:420`, `:438`
  - `store/db/postgres/user_delete.go:383`, `:401`
- Evidence there is *no* DB-level rule: the `reaction` table is declared with no foreign keys/cascade in any dialect — `store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:92-99`, `store/migration/postgres/LATEST.sql:91-98`, `store/migration/mysql/0.20/00__reaction.sql:2-9`. The only `ON DELETE CASCADE` in `LATEST.sql` is on `memo_share.memo_id` (`store/migration/sqlite/LATEST.sql:109`).

**h06** — handlers: `CreateMemo`, `UpdateMemo`, `DeleteMemo`, `CreateMemoComment`; convergence function: `webhook.Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`

| handler | dispatch call |
|---|---|
| `APIV1Service.CreateMemo` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70`) | `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` at `memo_service.go:157` |
| `APIV1Service.UpdateMemo` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:401`) | via `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` → `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` at `memo_update_helpers.go:67` |
| `APIV1Service.DeleteMemo` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:518`) | `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` at `memo_service.go:562` |
| `APIV1Service.CreateMemoComment` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:20`) | `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` at `memo_service_comments.go:119` |

All four funnel through `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook`/`DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` → `webhook.PostAsync` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:184`) → queue → **`webhook.Post`** (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:120`), the single function that issues the HTTP request to the user-configured `hook.Url`.

**h07**

```
GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar        — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124 (route)
FileServerService.serveUserAvatar         — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168
FileServerService.getUserByUsername       — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715
Store.GetUser                             — store/user.go:146 (checks userCache, then ListUsers)
Store.ListUsers → driver.ListUsers        — store/user.go (Driver iface: store/driver.go:10)
(*sqlite.DB).ListUsers                    — store/db/sqlite/user.go:159 (SELECT ... avatar_url ...)
```
The avatar bytes are stored inline on `user.avatar_url` as a data URI, decoded by `parseDataURI` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737`) and MIME-allowlisted via `avatarAllowedTypes` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:75`, checked at `:201`) before `c.Blob` at `:208`.

**h08** — two declarers

| declarer | invoked from production? | caller |
|---|---|---|
| `s3presign.Runner.RunOnce` — `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43` | yes | `Server.startBackgroundRunners` (`server/server.go:163`) and its own ticker loop `Run` (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36`) |
| `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27` | no | no callers anywhere (incl. tests); `memopayload.NewRunner` (`:19`) is likewise never called. Only the package-level `RebuildMemoPayload` (`:74`) is used in production (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`, `:447`). |

**h09** — 8 declarations total (6 non-test backend + 2 test helpers)

Declarations: `store/db/postgres/postgres.go:46`, `store/db/mysql/mysql.go:47`, `store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:67`, `store/store.go:72`, `server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:99`, `store/cache/cache.go:187`, plus test-only `store/test/filter_helpers_test.go:200` and `:282`.

Invoked by non-test server code:
- `store.Store.Close` — caller `Server.Shutdown`, `server/server.go:146`
- `cache.Cache.Close` — caller `Store.Close`, `store/store.go:74-76` (three caches)
- `store.Driver.Close` → the selected driver's `DB.Close` (`sqlite/sqlite.go:67` on a default install; `mysql/mysql.go:47`, `postgres/postgres.go:46` otherwise) — caller `Store.Close`, `store/store.go:78`
- `apiv1.SSEHub.Close` — caller `Server.closeLongLivedConnections`, `server/server.go:206`

**h10** — `(*filter.Engine).CompileToStatement` — `internal/filter/engine.go:74` — ~36 inbound calls (6 production + ~30 tests)

Production callers: `internal/filter/helpers.go`, `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go`, `server/router/api/v1/shortcut_service.go`, and `store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/memo_relation.go`. Runner-up: `(filter.Schema).Field` (`internal/filter/schema.go:67`) at ~21 calls, all inside `internal/filter`. Note: raw name-based counts put `Len` (180) and `Next` (57) on top, but those are name collisions with `require.Len` and `sql.Rows.Next` — not calls to `internal/version.SortVersion.Len` / `internal/scheduler.Schedule.Next`.

**h11** — 1st: `store.User`; 2nd: `store.Memo`

- `store.User` — referenced from 11 packages outside `store` (6 excluding `store/db/*`): `server/auth`, `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/api/v1/test`, `server/router/fileserver`, `server/router/rss`, plus `store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}` and test packages. Declared `store/user.go:29`.
- `store.Memo` — 10 packages (4 excluding `store/db/*`): `server/notification`, `server/router/api/v1`, `server/router/rss`, `server/runner/memopayload`. Declared `store/memo.go:35`.
- Next: `store.Attachment` (8), `store.Inbox`/`store.MemoRelation`/`store.MemoShare` (7 each).

**h12** — concrete method: `(*sqlite.DB).CreateMemo` — `store/db/sqlite/memo.go:16` (INSERT built at `:41`, executed at `:42`)

Determination: `Profile.Driver` defaults to `"sqlite"` in both the viper default and the flag (`cmd/memos/main.go:122`, `:130`), read into the profile at `cmd/memos/main.go:43`. That profile goes to `db.NewDBDriver` (`cmd/memos/main.go:57`), whose `switch profile.Driver` (`store/db/db.go:18-26`) picks `sqlite.NewDB` for the default. The resulting `store.Driver` is stored on `Store.driver` (`store/store.go:15`, `store.New` at `:38`), so `Store.CreateMemo`'s interface call on `store.Driver.CreateMemo` (`store/driver.go:10`) dispatches to the sqlite implementation. The other two candidates are `store/db/mysql/memo.go` and `store/db/postgres/memo.go`, reachable only with `--driver mysql|postgres`.

**h13** — impl: unexported `*markdown.service` — construction: `markdown.NewService(...)` at `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48` — holders: `APIV1Service`, `RSSService`, `memopayload.Runner`

- Interface `markdown.Service` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:31-55`); the only implementation is `type service struct` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:59`), returned by `NewService` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go:83-109`) with `WithTagExtension`/`WithMentionExtension` options.
- Production construction happens exactly once, at `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:48`; that single instance is stored on `APIV1Service.MarkdownService` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:35`) and passed to `rss.NewRSSService` (`server/server.go:85` → field at `server/router/rss/rss.go:45`). `memopayload.Runner` also declares the field (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:16`) but is never constructed in production (see h08). Tests build a second instance at `server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:44`.

**h14**

- Computation site: `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` — `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:74`, which delegates to `(*service).ExtractAll` — `internal/markdown/markdown.go:356`, a single goldmark AST walk.
- Triggers: `APIV1Service.CreateMemo` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`) and the memo-update path when content changes (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:447`, within `UpdateMemo`). The batch backfill `memopayload.Runner.RunOnce` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:52`) would also trigger it but is not wired into the server (h08).
- Extracted and written to `memo.Payload` (`server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:85-86`): `Tags` (all `#tag` nodes) and `Property` — `Title` (text of a leading H1, `internal/markdown/markdown.go:384-389`), `HasLink` (`:394`), `HasCode` (code block/fenced/span, `:397`), `HasTaskList` (`:400`), `HasIncompleteTasks` (unchecked task box, `:403`). `Mentions` is also collected by `ExtractAll` (`:380`) but consumed separately by `resolveMentionTargets` (`server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:32`) rather than stored on the payload.

```
APIV1Service.checkMemoReadAccess          — server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:39 (checks :55-65)
APIV1Service.ListMemos (visibility filter)— server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:178 (:219-225)
APIV1Service.CreateMemoComment            — server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:20 (:41, :100)
APIV1Service.ListMemoReactions / UpsertMemoReaction — server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:15 (:30-38), :83
APIV1Service.checkAttachmentAccess        — server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:422 (:445-451)
APIV1Service.ListMemoAttachments          — server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:200 (:214-222)
APIV1Service.resolveMentionTargets/notify — server/router/api/v1/memo_mention_helpers.go:62, :67
APIV1Service.<user notifications>         — server/router/api/v1/user_service_notifications.go:309-312
user memo-stats visibility filter         — server/router/api/v1/user_service_stats.go:84-90, :218-220
SSEClient.canReceive (event delivery)     — server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:134 (:135-141)
FileServerService.checkAttachmentPermission — server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:650 (:677-699)
RSSService.GetExploreRSS / user RSS       — server/router/rss/rss.go:90, :141 (PUBLIC only)

```

**r01** — False premise: there is no Redis anywhere in this codebase (no `redis` import, dependency, or config key).

Actual mechanism: an in-process, in-memory cache — `store/cache/cache.go`, a `sync.Map`-backed `Cache` with per-item expiry and a background `cleanupLoop`. `Store` holds three of them (`instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache`) at `store/store.go:27-29`, all constructed in `store.New` with one shared `cache.Config` (`store/store.go:40-53`): `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`, `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`, `MaxItems: 1000`. User entries are written with `Set` (`store/user.go:98`, `:122`, `:132`, `:143`, `:167`), and `Set` applies `c.config.DefaultTTL` (`store/cache/cache.go:92-94`) — so **10 minutes** for user entries. They are also invalidated eagerly on delete (`store/user_delete.go:40`).

**r02** — False premise: there is no rate-limiting middleware in this codebase, per-user or otherwise.

No rate-limit/throttle middleware is registered. Echo middleware on the server is only `middleware.Recover()` and a CORS middleware (`server/server.go:51-52`); the Connect/gRPC interceptor chain (`server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go`) does auth and logging, not throttling. The only occurrence of the phrase in Go source is an aspirational doc comment, `internal/email/doc.go:86` ("Rate limit email sending to prevent abuse"). The one bounded-throughput mechanism that exists is unrelated to API requests: a `semaphore.Weighted` capping concurrent thumbnail generation (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:107`).

**r03** — False premise: no cron scheduler is running, and no nightly database-cleanup job exists.

`internal/scheduler` is a complete cron-scheduler package (`internal/scheduler/scheduler.go`, `job.go`, `parser.go`, `middleware.go`) but it is **never imported** — a repo-wide search for `internal/scheduler` outside the package itself returns nothing. The string `"0 2 * * *"` with a `daily-cleanup` job appears only as illustrative example code in the package doc comment (`internal/scheduler/doc.go:14-21`), not as a registered job. The only background work the server actually starts is the 12-hour S3 presign runner (`server/server.go:153-174`, see h01).

**r04** — False premise: neither NATS nor RabbitMQ (nor any message broker) is used; there is no queue declaration.

Actual mechanism: an in-process Go channel. `asyncPostQueue` is a buffered channel of capacity 128 (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`), drained by 4 goroutines started in `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`), each calling `Post` (`:46`). Producers call `PostAsync` (`:184`), which does a non-blocking send and **drops** the webhook with a warning when the buffer is full (`:189-195`). Delivery is best-effort in-memory only — nothing is persisted, so queued webhooks are lost on restart.

**r05** — False premise: there is no GraphQL schema or GraphQL server in this codebase.

Actual API surface: Protobuf/gRPC defined under `proto/api/v1/*.proto` (generated to `proto/gen/api/v1/`), served over **Connect RPC** plus a **gRPC-gateway REST/JSON transcoding** layer registered at `apiV1Service.RegisterGateway(ctx, echoServer)` (`server/server.go:88`); handler wiring in `server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go` and `connect_services.go`. Alongside it are plain HTTP routes: `/file/...` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:122-124`), RSS (`server/router/rss/rss.go`), an SSE endpoint (`server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`), MCP (`server/router/mcp`), and `/healthz` (`server/server.go:67`).
